newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Cargill's N.Korean wheat seen heading for S.E.Asia.
newsitem.headline: Cargill's N.Korean wheat seen heading for S.E.Asia.

text.p: U.S. grain giant Cargill's shipment of 20,000 tonnes of wheat originally destined for North Korea is thought to be headed for Southeast Asia or Sri Lanka after the collapse of a zinc-for-wheat barter, traders said on Monday.
"Cargill's 20,000 tonnes of wheat is believed to be destined for a Southeast Asian country, possibly Indonesia, Sri Lanka or the Philippines," a trade source said.
Cargill declined to comment on the reports.
A trader with a flour mill said South Korean millers, who normally keep their silos full, did not have enough extra storage capacity to accept prompt delivery of the 20,000 tonnes.
He added that South Korea usually buy three types of U.S. wheat including No. 1 western white soft wheat, hard red winter wheat and dark northern spring wheat.
"Cargill's 20,000 tonnes of wheat was said to have been just one type. Furthermore, no local flour miller has the capacity to keep that amount in its own silos," the trader said.
He said the situation was similar in Taiwan and Japan.
Last Thursday, a Cargill spokeswoman in Washington said North Korea had cancelled the barter deal. No reason was given for the cancellation.
